newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat, barley ease after EU grain bids.
newsitem.headline: French wheat, barley ease after EU grain bids.

text.p: Wheat and barley prices eased on Thursday although traders bid massively in France to export EU wheat and barley at subsidies in this week's EU grain tenders, dealers said.
Rouen wheat for October-December delivery shed five francs to 885-890 francs while Rouen barley for October-December delivery dropped 10 francs to 870 francs.
Export prospects helped to support prices earlier this week. Grain industry sources stressed the lowest subsidy bids involved only small tonnages.
Traders bid in France to export 657,750 tonnes of EU free-market soft wheat at refunds ranging from 4.47 to 12.99 Ecus per tonne.
They also asked to export 496,000 tonnes of free-market EU barley at refunds ranging from 29.77 to 38.47 Ecus.
But the bids for the lowest subsidies were for only 1,000 tonnes of wheat and 25,000 tonnes of barley.
Reports Saudi Arabia had bought about 1.4 million tonnes of feed barley, helped boost French barley prices earlier this week.
EU barley is widely expected to help cover a large part of the contract.

France, which has set an ambitious export target for its barley for the new 1996/97 season, hopes to get a sizeable share of the deal if the Commission continues to grant exports of free-market barley with subsidies. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
